narrative:
The model estimates there’s a 66% chance you won’t pass your final year, which is well above the 10% threshold that requires extra help. Because of this, you’ll need to take remedial courses to improve your chances.

The main reason the model is concerned is that you’ve already failed a class before. Students who’ve never failed tend to pass, so this single factor is the strongest signal that you’re at risk. The second biggest concern is why you chose this school: most students who picked it for its reputation or because it was close to home are doing better, while those who came mainly for a specific course—like you did—often struggle more. On a positive note, the model sees that you still want to go to university, and that ambition is actually helping your outlook a little.

Other parts of your situation also played a role. Your parents’ education level is lower than most of your classmates’, and you don’t have internet at home, which makes studying harder. You also spend less than two hours a week on schoolwork, while most students who pass put in more time. On the other hand, you’ve never missed school, and your health is very good, which helps.

The remedial courses will give you extra time and support to catch up. Focus on the subjects you’ve struggled with before, and try to increase your study time. If you can, find a way to get online—even borrowing a device or using the school library—so you can access more learning materials. Your goal of going to university is still within reach, but you’ll need to make these changes now.
